title: Filtering requests and filtering a customer total are different questions
goal: Distinguish dataset parameters, detail filters and aggregate conditions using discriminating input.

prerequisites.text: Complete P1–P8. Distinguish a common-module function from its application caller; preserve your source and run a separate training infobase.

sections.title: The question we are checking
paragraphs: Two jobs took 25 minutes each. Neither exceeds 40, but together they total 50. Does the report need long jobs or customers with a large combined duration? The order of operations changes the answer.
Use a new training copy and invented records only. Predict first, then compare the observation; preserve existing functions, files, and records.

paragraphs: Continue your own P8 copy. Close Enterprise, save a DT backup and restore it into a new empty infobase; verify the actual path. Preserve prior work, records and the handler. Do not load a full CF over your work.

sections.title: Filter level changes meaning
paragraphs: Filtering rows before aggregation differs from filtering groups after it. “Requests longer than 30 minutes” is not “customers totaling more than 30.” A customer with two short requests distinguishes them. Settings must express the intended requirement.

The previous source retains the own-customer filter and applies minutes>30 to detail:30/45 yields 45. Moving the condition to sum(minutes)>30 is different: the customer total 75 includes both documents.

paragraphs: УчебныеОтчёты common module: Server and Server call enabled; Client, Global, and Privileged disabled. Functions are outside procedures. The application module has one handler that calls the function and displays labelled result fields.

sections.title: The application call and its observation
paragraphs: For the worked 30/45 dataset, filtering details >30 leaves 45. The other path actually groups in DCS with a sum resource to obtain 75, then our explicit code applies >30 to that composed total. It does not silently change a quick-filter panel: both boundaries appear in the function.
Each message is labelled: identical Да values concern different assertions. Find the expression behind each line and distinguish its truth from the fact that the program ran.

The schema resource defines the minute sum and DCS settings group by customer. In this source, own code tests the resulting aggregate after composition; it is not an existing quick-filter control in the report UI.

sections.title: Parameters fix computation
paragraphs: Supply virtual-table period, customer and status with correct types. A dynamic CurrentMonth parameter is convenient operationally but should be fixed for reproducible evidence. Avoid hidden conditions lost on reopening. A saved variant must restore every material value.

Source-period parameters constrain input before aggregation. Detail filters and group-total conditions act at different levels. The original report has a quick Customer filter; do not describe period/status quick fields as already implemented.

sections.title: Your prediction first
paragraphs: Must both paths return the same minutes for 30/45?
Identify the changed action and what should remain unchanged. Reveal the explanation after making your own prediction.

reveal.title: Check the reasoning
paragraphs: No. The first path excludes 30 before summing. The second includes both requests in 75 and then checks that total. The unit remains minutes.

sections.title: Grouping does not change units
paragraphs: Customer minute sums remain minutes. For a per-document average, specify numerator and denominator; an average of group averages generally differs from the global average. Use customers with unequal request counts as a control. Apply rounding at the declared point.

In Designer open Reports → ЗаявкиПоКлиентам → Templates → main DCS template. Inspect Datasets, Resources and Settings. Retain the primary variant and create an own variant named by intent, such as Details above 30.

sections.title: Trace preservation step by step
paragraphs: This diagram shows only the group path. Compare it with 30/45 → detail >30 → 45; the detail path does not run before this one. Our code applies the total condition after composition; it is not presented as a ready-made UI setting.
Read each arrow: what value or relation exists now, and which action changes it? The diagram explains the selected property rather than replacing the source.

sections.title: An error that can look successful
paragraphs: Filtering the 25/25 details >40 and calling the result “customers totalling >40” removes both rows before summation and loses the valid 50 total. Renaming the report does not repair the selected level.
Keep the faulty copy separate. To establish a fix, compare the relevant observation with your prior expectation; do not change an expectation merely to obtain a match.

sections.title: Tests distinguish similar reports
paragraphs: Compare rows>30, groups>30, average and sum on one set. Specify expected identities and values beforehand, then save/reopen the variant. A missing-filter negative control must fail. If every variant accidentally yields one number, the dataset does not distinguish wrong implementations and must expand.

Reconcile all facts 75, details>30 → 45 and group total>30 → 75. Equal totals on another dataset do not prove equivalent rules. Add another own customer with 20/20: no detail exceeds 30, but its total 40 does.

sections.title: Now a new independent task
paragraphs: Implement your own function for two new 25-minute requests belonging to your customer. A detail filter >40 must yield 0 rows/0 minutes. Separately obtain an actual DCS group and apply your own condition to its total: >40 gives 1 group/50 minutes; >50 gives 0 groups. Do not add totals to detail rows, and check your own customer key.
